quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the crossing guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a crossing guard tells you to. Always drive slowly and safely in school zones.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
Honk your horn before passing on the left side.
Keep driving when you think most children have left the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is put away.

questions.question: Always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Parking or leaving a parking space.
Entering traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, parking, leaving a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals tell other drivers what you are doing and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should take care of your physical health by:

options.text: Staying in good physical condition and getting regular check-ups.
Understanding how medicine affects your driving.
Driving only within what your body can handle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your health affects how well you can drive. Know your physical limits and only drive if it is safe.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a distraction and can cause a crash.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are turning.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times when driving.

questions.question: Signaling before you turn, change lanes, or pull away from the curb:

options.text: Is only necessary if other cars are near.
Is a good habit and the law requires it.
Is only needed during the move, not before.
Is not required if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle right or left. Always signal before pulling away from the curb.

questions.question: Do not pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a hill or around a curve.
When a school bus has flashing lights.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see clearly, at intersections, near railroad crossings, on bridges, when a school bus has red flashing lights, or in any no passing zone.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help them feel normal again?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when:

options.text: You stare straight ahead at the road for too long.
You take many rest stops.
You get too much sleep the night before driving.
You drive short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare straight ahead at the road for too long.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare ahead without looking around. You stop paying attention and can easily crash into traffic ahead of you.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: The driver only.
Passengers on long trips.
All people in a car on expressways.
All people in a car every time it is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All people in a car every time it is driven.
questions.explanation: Every person in your car should wear a seat belt at all times. Without a seat belt, a person can be thrown around inside the car during a crash and hurt other people.

questions.question: Which of these can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and other alcohol
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many things can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications such as prescription and over-the-counter drugs.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should change your driving when weather changes suddenly.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden weather changes mean you need to adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Watch especially for fast vehicles behind you that may not be going slow enough for the conditions.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signals, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let that vehicle pass safely before you go.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
No right turn allowed.
All traffic must go straight.
A road is joining from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road is joining from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead. A road will join from the right side.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter drug should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive anyway even if there are warnings.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings before driving. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if the medicine is safe to take while driving.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, use ____ to show you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers when you are turning.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is best described as:

options.text: Your tires pushing water out of the way.
Your tires sliding on a layer of water.
Your tires splashing water on other cars.
Your tires throwing water backward at following vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires sliding on a layer of water.
questions.explanation: When roads are wet, tires have good grip up to about 35 mph. As you go faster, your tires may leave the road and slide on a thin layer of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Get your papers ready before the officer reaches you.
Stay in your car with your hands on the wheel. Wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the wheel. Wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to exit. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, what must you do?

options.text: Stop immediately where you are.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Pull over to the right side of the road.
Speed up and stay out of the emergency vehicle's way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. When you see or hear a police car, fire truck, or ambulance with lights and sirens, pull to the right edge of the road as quickly as you can.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed.
Road work is happening ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work is happening ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction zones. This sign tells you that road work is ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Before you change lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot to make sure no one is there.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
People walking.
Other cars.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: People walking.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: What is important to remember about trucks on the road?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
They pass faster going downhill than smaller vehicles.
They turn with a smaller radius than smaller vehicles.
They pass faster going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if you can do it without damaging the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways carefully.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: When red lights flash and bells ring at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Do not go around or under the gate. Wait until the lights stop and the gate is fully up before crossing.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Keep your tires properly filled with air.
Drive slower in the rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper air pressure. Also drive slower in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds when it is wet.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep going, but only if there are no vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is near.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going, but only if there are no vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection go first. You can keep going if the intersection is clear, but be ready to stop if the light changes.

questions.question: What should you do when you meet an aggressive driver?

options.text: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Follow them closely.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm around aggressive drivers. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make rude gestures. Try to put distance between your car and theirs.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than any train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around the gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad warning signs tell you a train might be nearby. Always follow these signs and never go around barriers or ignore them.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal whenever you move your vehicle left or right. This includes entering traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Your current road ends ahead.
You must bear either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must choose to bear either right or left.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving ability?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.
